title: LSTM and GRU
overview: Gated recurrent cells control what to remember and forget, giving gradients a more stable path through time. LSTM and GRU are the standard recurrent building blocks.
objectives: Describe the LSTM gates and cell state
Pick between them for a task

method.title: LSTM cell state
method.body: A separate cell state c_t is updated additively, which helps gradients survive long spans.

method.title: Gates
method.body: Forget, input and output gates, each a sigmoid, decide what to erase, write and expose.

method.title: GRU
method.body: Merges the cell and hidden state and uses only update and reset gates, so it has fewer parameters.

method.title: Practice
method.body: Performance is often similar; GRU is lighter, LSTM sometimes better on long sequences.

pseudocode:
f = sigmoid(Wf @ [h, x] + bf)
i = sigmoid(Wi @ [h, x] + bi)
o = sigmoid(Wo @ [h, x] + bo)
g = tanh(Wg @ [h, x] + bg)
c = f * c + i * g
h = o * tanh(c)

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
sig = lambda z: 1 / (1 + np.exp(-z))
d, hdim = 3, 4
W = {k: rng.normal(size=(d + hdim, hdim)) * 0.4 for k in "fiog"}
h = np.zeros(hdim); c = np.zeros(hdim)
for x in rng.normal(size=(3, d)):
    z = np.concatenate([x, h])
    f, i, o = sig(z @ W["f"]), sig(z @ W["i"]), sig(z @ W["o"])
    g = np.tanh(z @ W["g"])
    c = f * c + i * g
    h = o * np.tanh(c)
print("h:", np.round(h, 3))
print("c:", np.round(c, 3))
